Hopefully it was clear that I wasn't being serious, but merely silly in my overly-PC-elitist comment.  (Side note: we really need a good/obvious smiley for that on this forum… the   is a little hard to tell apart from just an open mouth smile).

The truth is I do prefer a computer for gaming, but that's largely because I mostly play RTS's or FPS's… RTS's just don't work on console, and nothing will ever convince me that a dual-stick controller is better than a mouse+keyboard for an FPS.  (For some 3rd-person games I love a controller, so I'm not saying controllers are inherently bad).  I also like consoles, though mostly for split-screen group play where you're all in the same room.  The various portable gaming systems haven't interested me in like 15 years, but that's largely because I drive to work and can't game en route, and given the choice between playing some game on a small screen or my TV/computer, the TV/computer are going to win every time.  (And yes, I'm aware that the Switch can be connected to a TV, which is a fact that has led me to almost purchasing it a few times).

All that to say, I prefer computers, but certainly don't actually fault anyone for liking consoles/portables and in fact like them myself.

A couple of updates:

-Wraith got her own side-quest, where you must infiltrate a FILTER base filled with overwhelming opposition (using only Wraith, from what I understood) to get some secret files they have on the heroes. This unlocks her Stealth-Suit, which gives her more stealth and agility but has less offensive options. 

-Console-upgrade option, where those who pledged 30$+ can choose to get a copy of the game for PS4 or Xbox instead of PC/Mac.  

 

 

I'm very interested on the Stealth-Suit and how it affects the game. I love the possibility of non-combat focused characters, but I'm afraid they can turn out to be pretty useless if you can only get things done by knocking out dudes. The image of getting Wraith sneaking around the battlefield and flanking enemies/getting to important objectives is really cool, but there's also thig chance of her not getting to do anything significant after getting there (due to lack of firepower). 

But I'm just wondering about things I have little information on. Anyways, I hope the game gets more interesting missions like this, where the objective isn't just knocking out all the dudes (although it will help a lot).

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
Hmm - the example of dropping a car might not be too hard, because essentially all it is is destroying a destructible bit of the environment and then doing damage to a character, maybe also re-instantiating the bit of the environment if possible, with appropriate animations.

Reacting to a ranged attack seemed trickier to me at first, until I remembered that Underbite is building in a complex set of reaction behaviors beyond the typical overwatch. Maybe there’s just a “reaction: portal redirection” button you hit, and then the first enemy in sight of your guy who launches a ranged attack gets portalified. The actual appearance of portal shenanigans would, again, occur in the animation domain.

Not to say that all this would be SIMPLE to do, but it strikes me that this stuff doesn’t have to be any harder in the SoF engine than building the action and animation set for any other super powered character. I mean, we already know that Bunker has to animate between different appearances with different abilities, Tachyon has a unique movement animation, and there are advanced features for the different effects that can happen in a character (distraction, reaction, getting to cover, etc).

This all leads me to wonder: when we create a character, there’s a lot we can customize about their background and personality. But how does customizing the power set, and the actions available in the game, work? Can I make a spaceship for Trajector, Space Fighter Pilot to warp in and fly? Can Rabit make his portaler? Do we choose a “power archetype” from a limited set (speedster, brawler, etc) and that determines all the in-game actions and animations for our character, or do we build a custom set of actions and choose animations for each action? Are our character’s animations canned, procedurally generated, or do we get access to the rigging in the character creator?

I just ask all these questions because I’m excited.
